native_source_families.meaning: makes two float-binding calls, then toggles one of two global flag bytes selected by an object field and returns bit 6 of the flag word
makes two float-binding calls, then toggles one of two global flag bytes selected by an object field and returns bit 6 of the flag word
Build a 32-byte packet of four packed 64-bit cursor words from two resident cursor globals and four indices, then hand it to the recorder with the caller's second payload word.
Reset seven embedded sub-objects of one structure in a row, then walk seven 72-byte records from +536 clearing each through the pair helper, and return the structure.

When a predicate on the embedded sub-object at +32 returns zero, add the float at sub-object +4 to the float at +12 and, while the word at +32 is below six, rewrite the top byte of the word at +4 with a scaled fraction; otherwise call the fallback helper on the object.
Dissolve one object: return immediately when its word at +1160 is zero, otherwise call teardown helpers on the object and on eight embedded sub-objects at fixed offsets.

Calls a three-argument callee twice and a two-argument callee twice over fields of the first object, folds a float field through a float-to-int callee into an int field of the object, and calls a last callee when the updated field is negative.

Reads one byte and one pointer from a shared global; returns a callee float when the byte is zero, returns 0.0f when the byte is outside 0..2, otherwise fills three stack locals through three callees and returns the last callee float.

Forwards one shared global pointer plus a fixed byte offset, together with five distinct fixed offsets of the first object, into the same callee five times, reading one distinct word of the second object each call.

Resets a record through a three-pointer helper, folds a float at offset 0x30 into the float at 0xc, increments the byte at 8, decrements the 16-bit counter at 10 and, when it reaches zero, adds 0xff000000 to the word at 4 and refills the counter with 2; then calls a helper when the top byte of the word at 4 is clear.

Stores the third argument at offset 0x1564; when the word at 0x1568 is non-zero it clears it, calls five helpers on fields at 0xf1c/0xfb0/0x1044/0x10d8/0x1160 with second arguments 0,0,0,1,0 and then a two-float helper on the block at 0x148; finally repeats that two-float call when the word at 0x157c is non-zero.
Calls sixteen one-argument helpers with a base pointer plus fixed offsets 0,0x4c,0x98,0xe4,0x130,0x17c,0x1c8,0x210,0x258,0x2a0,0x2e8,0x330,0x378,0x3b4,0x400,0x44c and returns that base pointer.

Refreshes a child sub-structure through a setup helper, folds four float pairs (one measured against a fixed half-turn constant) through a shared two-float helper, and hands the resulting four-field block to a second helper.
Tests the handle cached in the object and, while the handle reports itself already released, drops the next sub-handle, otherwise runs the object's destroy helper.
Resets eleven inline sub-blocks of one object through two helpers, three of them reached by a three-iteration countdown loop over a 76-byte stride, then returns the object pointer.

Applies one shared blend factor to two adjacent sub-blocks through two helper calls, advances a float timer field by a fixed step, then either packs a small counter into a tagged word or runs a reset helper.

calls a setup routine, then when the third parameter is non-null allocates a 16-byte record through two callees, stores it in the context at +52 and zeroes its four words; zeroes the first two words of that record re-reading the context field and writes 100.0f into both words of the pointer at context+0 and 64.0f into both words of the pointer at context+4, then clears context+56

looks up a 112-byte record in a fixed global table by the index returned by a callee, bounds-checks the index against a byte count reached through two pointer hops, stores the index and a context pointer into the record and returns the callee's index or -1

Guarded re-initialiser: when the record word at +44 is non-zero it allocates and zeroes two 16-byte blocks through a helper pair and stores them at +52 and +56, resets three floats of the object reached through +4 to 1.0, and always clears the words at +72 and +68.

Guarded fixed-descendant initialiser: when the record word at +1080 is non-zero it calls four initialisers on sub-objects at 76-byte steps from the record, then one two-argument call on the sub-object at +528, five whole-record helpers and a final initialiser on the sub-object at +380.

Walks 120 records of 64 bytes from a base resolved through two descriptor lookups; for each live record it calls an update helper and, when that reports zero, counts it and advances a float pair by one step, clearing the record's live flag otherwise.

Walks up to 25 records of 10 bytes; for each record whose 16-bit key is non-negative and whose table byte is set, resolves an object through a helper and copies/relocates it with the record's 16-bit length, capping the destination table at 25 entries.

Three-attempt retry helper: the float argument is compared against 0.5 and picks which of two argument triples is tried first; a non-zero result returns at once, and the third call (always with the first triple) is emitted once and jumped to from both branches.

Selects a 72-byte record with the second argument, asks a helper twice for a scratch vector and writes the float conversions of the third and fourth arguments into its first two slots, feeds the fifth argument (and its top byte) to three further calls, and tail-calls the virtual function at offset 12 of the object reached through the record's pointer at +48 with the record advanced by that object's signed 16-bit field at +8.

Walks the three columns of a four-float-wide row array, gathering each column into a four-element local whose fourth element is zeroed, passing that local twice plus 1.0f to a call and scattering the result back into the same column.

Switches on a state byte of the sub-object 32 bytes into the record, adds three floats read through that sub-object's pointer into the record's own three floats when the state is 2, updates the high byte of a 24-bit/8-bit packed counter from a signed 16-bit field, and forwards the record 16 bytes ahead through a second call when a flag byte is set.

Returns immediately when the word at object+1024 is zero; otherwise clears two sub-blocks, runs two marker calls and two zero-argument helpers, then clears two more sub-blocks and nine further 72-byte strided sub-blocks up to +888.

Reads a signed halfword state and a paired halfword; returns when the state is non-zero and the pair is already cleared, otherwise clamps a halfword counter (minimum 1) scaled by state/limit, or asks a helper to fill three bytes when the state is zero.
Dispatches on a byte mode at object+32: mode 0 updates two float angles from a linked node and runs a follow-up call; mode 1 refreshes a 16-byte block and a node copy then calls a final update.
Call the registered handler with a table pointer built from one module base word plus the constant 36808, forwarding the incoming argument; do nothing when the base word is zero.

Walks five 76-byte-strided descriptor slots: when the header short is nonzero it calls through the function pointer at +12 of the word loaded from the +60 cursor, passing the +12 cursor plus the signed short at +8; then conditionally releases up to three fixed sub-objects at +408/+552/+480 guarded by the words at +656/+660/+668/+664.

Programs a memory-mapped DMA channel in two phases: each phase spins while bit 0x100 of the fixed control word 0x10008000 stays set, calling a 16-unit delay helper, then stores into three fixed registers (0x10008020 = 0, 0x10008030 = arg & 0x0FFFFFFF, 0x10008000 = 325).

calls a probe on field +10; when it returns zero it repacks the high byte of the int at +4 from the byte at +52, fills a four-float stack block from +32/+36/+40 and zero, passes it to a call with +16 twice, then adds byte +53 into byte +8, adds float +48 into float +12 and subtracts float +44 from float +40

takes the float array at +104 and writes four values returned by a call with argument 255, then four float constants (-1.0, -2.25, 1.25, 2.5) at +16..+28, a descending count 255/191/127/63 into the ints at +44..+32 and 2.5/3.0 pairs at +48..+60
